hook: Antisense drugs fixing one UNC13A splicing error restore synapse function in TDP-43-depleted neurons.
summary: Losing TDP-43 leaves neurons intact but with failing synaptic communication, and correcting a single cryptic splicing event in UNC13A rescued this. Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides restored vesicle release and network synchrony in human cortical and motor neurons, and worked in a humanized mouse model. Benefit in patients is untested, and the work covers cultured neurons and mice.
title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss.
